The Brief
“

Making dense logistics logic read clearly at a glance, without the product turning into a spreadsheet.

An internal tool, built for people who use it all day.

Salasa runs a logistics operation that lives or dies on fast, accurate decisions — which carrier gets an order, what a merchant gets charged, whether a shipment is on track. They needed an internal platform that could keep up with that pace.

Our product team designed and built it end to end, turning a moving set of logistics requirements into one interface their operations staff could actually work in, every day. The hard part was never the screens — it was making dense logistics logic read clearly at a glance.

This case study uses recreated, portfolio-safe screens with placeholder data. No confidential operational information is shown.
1
Architecture that scales

A maintainable frontend foundation — reusable components, predictable state, patterns the whole team could build on.

2
Complexity made usable

Carrier logic, pricing matrices and capacity rules, turned into interfaces operations staff can actually read.

3
Built for real use

Loading states, error recovery, validation and responsiveness — the details that make software usable eight hours a day.

The Product

A system operations teams live in every day.

Analytics, rules, pricing, operational tables and full decision transparency — curated to show the breadth of what shipped.

What It Does

Built for operational clarity at scale.

Every screen balances data density with scanability — fast access to the controls operations teams need, without the product becoming unreadable.

01
Order & Shipment Operations

Data grids, filters, order detail views and live shipment status updates.

02
Rule-Based Assignation

Dynamic logical conditions, priorities, fallbacks and a live decision preview.

03
Carrier Capacity

Carrier and account-level capacity with used and remaining visibility.

04
Merchant Pricing & Service Zones

Reusable zone definitions kept separate from merchant-specific rates, COD and weight rules.

05
Decision Observability

Assignation logs that make every routing outcome traceable and explainable.

06
Reusable Frontend System

Shared form controls, validation patterns, tables and feedback states used across the product.

The Team

Four disciplines, one product.

No solo build. Salasa OMS came out of a small cross-functional team, each person owning a different part of getting it right.

Frontend Engineering

Architected the interface from scratch — component system, data views, forms and state management for a genuinely complex product.

Product & UX Design

Shaped how dense logistics logic reads on screen — the difference between a usable tool and a wall of data.

Quality & Delivery

Owned edge cases, validation and the everyday reliability an internal tool needs to earn trust.

Product Direction

Turned shifting logistics requirements into a scope the team could actually ship, sprint after sprint.

How We Built It

Product thinking, not just pixel delivery.

Consistency

Shared primitives cut cognitive load across every module in the product.

Resilience

Every screen accounts for loading, empty, error and partial-data states — not just the happy path.

Performance

Caching, targeted fetching and pagination keep dense workflows fast.

Maintainability

Typed interfaces and a feature-first structure make a complex domain easier to extend.
